title: Synthesis of a La-based metal–organic framework and its utilization as a humidity sensor exhibiting superior sensing capabilities
content: In the current investigation, a Lanthanum-based metal–organic framework [La(BTC)]-MOF has been layered onto a pair of rectangular aluminium (Al) electrodes to create a combined capacitive and impedance-style humidity sensor (Al/[La(BTC)]-MOF/Al). The solution-processable [La(BTC)]-MOF was applied using a straightforward drop-casting method. The characterization of the structure and examination of the surface morphology of the active layer have been conducted using XRD, BET, FTIR, SEM and TEM techniques, respectively. The humidity assessment capabilities of the sensor have been evaluated by subjecting the [La(BTC)]-MOF active film to a broad spectrum of relative humidity (% RH) levels (38 – 88% RH) at ambient conditions. The designed sensor displays a remarkably enhanced average sensitivity of approximately 3.359 nF/% RH and –43.968 kΩ/% RH when functioning in capacitive and impedance modes, respectively. Furthermore, the humidity sensor demonstrates excellent reproducibility, and quick response (68 s) and recovery (54 s) times. The markedly improved sensing attributes indicate that the proposed sensor can be effectively utilized for real-time humidity monitoring in environmental settings.
